name: Separated Additions Can Cooperate
statement: For every integer $\ell\ge0$, there is a cornerless ample family $G_\ell$ of order $597+\ell$ and outside words $a_\ell,b_\ell$ such that $G_\ell$ and both one-tip extensions are nonpeelable, while $G_\ell\cup\{a_\ell,b_\ell\}$ is dismantlable ample. All four families are ample. The additions acquire disjoint four-coordinate supports, and their completed cubes have Hamming distance $8+\ell$. Each of the three nonpeelable families has Hall's cornerless obstruction as a proper pc-minor, so none is itself a forbidden pc-minor.
proof: Translate Hall's 299-concept cornerless family and a certified resolving tip so that the prescribed peeling of the repaired family ends at the attachment word zero. Take two copies on disjoint twelve-coordinate blocks and join their zero words by the monotone path $T_\ell=\{1^k0^{\ell-k}:0\le k\le\ell\}$. No mixed pair of coordinates is shattered, so the shadow is the union of the two block shadows and the $\ell$ bridge singletons. The Sandwich equality proves ampleness before and after either or both tips are added. Every old vertex remains a noncorner and every internal path vertex has two incident directions without a square, so the base is cornerless. Either one-tip extension retains the other Hall copy as a proper signed restriction and is nonpeelable. After both tips are added, peel each repaired Hall copy to its attachment and then peel the remaining path. The two completed four-cubes lie four steps from their respective attachments and differ across every bridge coordinate, giving distance $4+\ell+4$.
comments: The fixed certificate checks bridge lengths zero and three, including all four shadow equalities, cornerlessness, both proper Hall restrictions, completed-cube distances, and combined peelings of lengths 599 and 602. This refutes geometric separation as a substitute for pc-minimality; cooperation over a cornerless forbidden pc-minor remains open.
